whoDefines.heading: Who defines disability here?
body: Disability is not one fixed category, and a person may not use the word at all. Different systems use different definitions, so someone can meet one and not another.

For Medical Assistance in Minnesota, disability is certified by the Social Security Administration or, for people it has not certified, by the State Medical Review Team (SMRT) at the Department of Human Services. SMRT uses Social Security's criteria but looks at the medical condition only, not the ability to work. Schools and employers apply their own rules.

Ask what words the person uses, who gave them a label, and what that label has meant for them. When the person wants to talk about it, also ask what caused or worsened a condition, such as work, housing, migration or barriers to care.

sources.label: Minnesota DHS, The State Medical Review Team

whatTheLabelUnlocks.heading: What does the label unlock?
body: A disability certification is one step toward programs such as Medical Assistance, MA-TEFRA for children, Medical Assistance for Employed Persons with Disabilities, the disability waivers (Community Alternative Care, CADI, Brain Injury and Developmental Disability) and the Family Support Grant. Other applications and assessments may also be needed. A county or Tribal worker submits the SMRT request, and Disability Hub MN says the process can take from 6 weeks to a year.

A MnCHOICES assessment is used to determine eligibility for publicly funded long-term services and supports. Anyone can ask for one by calling their county or Tribal Nation, regardless of financial status, and can ask for an interpreter.

These rules were checked on October 30, 2026, and they change. The Department of Human Services owns current policy, so check its pages before relying on this summary. A label can open services and can also carry costs for the person. Ask what they want it to do.

routes.name: Disability Hub MN
routes.purpose: A free statewide resource network that helps people with disabilities solve problems and find their way through the service system. Phone 1-866-333-2466, chat or email.

routes.name: County or Tribal Nation: MnCHOICES assessment
routes.purpose: The starting point for long-term services and supports. Call the county or Tribal Nation to ask for an assessment, and ask for an interpreter if needed.

routes.name: Help Me Grow
routes.purpose: Minnesota's route to early intervention and preschool special education for children from birth through age 5 when there is a concern about development. Referrals go to the child's local school district: Infant and Toddler Intervention for birth through age 2, and Preschool Special Education for ages 3 to 5.

routes.name: Vocational Rehabilitation Services
routes.purpose: The state's employment services for people with disabilities, at the Department of Employment and Economic Development.

routes.name: DHS Deaf, DeafBlind and Hard of Hearing State Services
routes.purpose: Regional offices offering assistive technology information, DeafBlind services, interpreter lists and mental health referrals. Phone 1-800-657-3663.

routes.name: Minnesota Disability Law Center
routes.purpose: The state's Protection and Advocacy agency, part of Mid-Minnesota Legal Aid. Free legal help on disability rights issues, though it cannot take every case. Intake 1-877-696-6529.

routes.name: Ombudsman for Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities
routes.purpose: An independent state agency that takes complaints about services for mental illness and developmental disabilities, at no fee. Phone 1-800-657-3506.

routes.name: Minnesota Council on Disability
routes.purpose: State policy, training and technical resource on disability. Phone 1-800-945-8913.
